The mine tours have a short summer-only season with a handful of fixed departure times a day and they have changed hands in recent years: call or check before driving up rather than turning up, and treat the road and the view as the reason to go if the tour is not running. Tours are charged per person on top of the drive. Signal drops out north of North River.
items.needs_booking: advisable, check the day before for tour times

items.name: Route 8 west to Speculator
items.what: Route 8 runs past the end of the drive. Head west and it skirts the Siamese Ponds Wilderness, passes Eleventh Mountain, and picks up the East Branch of the Sacandaga with fishing pull-offs most of the way to Speculator. It is the emptiest road you can reach without trying.
items.note: Around an hour each way to Speculator, and longer than the map suggests. There is no fuel, no shop and no reliable phone signal between Bakers Mills and Route 30, so stock up in North Creek or Chestertown first. Frost heaves are bad from March into May and will rattle a loaded car. It is ploughed in winter, but there is little open at the far end in January, so there is no reward at the end of the drive.

items.name: Prospect Mountain Veterans Memorial Highway
items.what: A five-mile paved toll road climbing to a summit above Lake George, with a car park near the top and a short walk (a shuttle sometimes runs, but do not count on it) to the viewing area. The easiest big view in the region for anyone who cannot manage a hike.
items.note: Strictly seasonal: roughly late May to Veterans Day in November, weather permitting, and shut all winter. The fee is charged per vehicle rather than per head, in the region of ten dollars a car, so a full car is cheap — confirm the current rate. The gate closes in the late afternoon, earlier after Labor Day, so it is not a sunset drive. They close it for weather and cloud at short notice, so check on the morning rather than driving forty minutes on spec.

items.name: Cedar River Road and the Moose River Plains
items.what: A gravel wilderness road running west from Indian Lake past the Cedar River Flow into the Moose River Plains. Ponds, primitive campsites, and a real chance of seeing deer at dusk.
items.note: Gated and seasonal. It opens in late spring once the snow and mud have gone, often around Memorial Day but later in a slow year, and closes after big-game season in the autumn; in winter it is a snowmobile trail and nothing else. DEC publishes the complex page but not reliable gate dates, so ring the DEC Region 5 office listed on that page before setting out — a shut gate turns this into an hour and a half of driving for nothing. Unpaved and rough: not for a low car, carry a working spare, and expect no phone signal at all. The forty-five minutes above is to the start of the road, not to the far end.

items.name: North Creek
items.what: The nearest village and your default for anything you forgot. Fuel, a small grocery and general store, a few cafes and restaurants, outfitters, the Tannery Pond Center for concerts and theatre, and the restored 1871 depot where Theodore Roosevelt learned he had become president.
items.note: Nothing stays open late. Plan dinner before 8pm, and do not count on Sunday or Monday opening in the shoulder seasons of April, May and November. This is a top-up shop, not a big shop: the full supermarket is Chestertown or Warrensburg. The farmers market runs Thursday afternoons at Riverfront Park from roughly mid-June to mid-September. The scenic passenger train between Saratoga and North Creek stopped in 2018 and has not returned, whatever old listings suggest; what runs on the old line now is pedal-powered rail bikes from the station, which are popular and need booking. The depot museum keeps short summer hours, broadly early July to Labor Day and closed Wednesdays.

items.name: Chestertown
items.what: Crossroads village where Route 8 meets the Northway at exit 25. This is the errand town: a full supermarket on Route 9, hardware, liquor, a pharmacy counter, a fuel station that is reliably open, and a handful of places to eat. A farmers market runs at the town hall on summer Wednesdays.
items.note: Fifteen minutes each way, so consolidate into one shop rather than three trips. The supermarket keeps long hours seven days a week and is the most dependable food stop near the house. The Wednesday market runs roughly June to early September, mid-morning into the early afternoon. Restaurant hours contract sharply after Columbus Day and several places shut entirely for the spring mud season, so phone ahead in April and November rather than driving over.

items.name: Warrensburg and the World's Largest Garage Sale
items.what: The nearest large supermarket, pharmacy and hardware store, on the Schroon River. Once a year the whole town becomes a yard sale, with hundreds of vendors along Main Street and through the residential streets, on the first weekend of October. There is also a riverfront farmers market on Friday afternoons through the summer.
items.note: Garage Sale weekend is 2 to 4 October in 2026 and draws tens of thousands of people; check the official site for the date in later years. Route 9 and the Northway exits jam solid, so arrive before 9am or write the day off, and use the marked shuttle car parks rather than hunting for a space on Main Street. Free to attend, held rain or shine, and most sellers take cash only. Sales run sunup to sundown, not shop hours. The Friday farmers market runs late afternoon, roughly late May to early October.

items.name: Schroon Lake and the Seagle Festival
items.what: A quiet lake town with a free public beach, a short main street and an original Art Deco cinema showing first-run films. It is also home to the Seagle Festival, a long-established summer opera and musical theatre company that stages four mainstage productions across July and August, plus a children's show that tours nearby towns.
items.note: Seagle plays to a small house on a short run — each mainstage title runs only a few nights — and popular ones sell out, so book weeks ahead rather than turning up. The cinema is summer-only, broadly Memorial Day to Labor Day, has no website, and posts its schedule on Facebook, so do not plan a rainy-afternoon film in May or October. The Adirondack Marathon takes over the last weekend of September (27 September in 2026): the course circles the lake and roads are closed or down to one lane until mid-afternoon on the Sunday, and the Saturday 5K and 10K run in Chestertown. Good to watch, a real problem if you had planned to drive through.
items.needs_booking: advisable, two to four weeks ahead for Seagle performances

items.name: Blue Mountain Lake and the Adirondack Experience
items.what: A large museum of Adirondack life spread over a hillside above the lake: guideboats, logging, a one-room schoolhouse, rustic furniture, and good hands-on exhibits for children. The drive over from Indian Lake on Route 28 is one of the better ones in its own right.
items.note: Open daily from roughly late May to mid-October and shut the rest of the year, so it is not a winter or early-spring fallback. Allow three to four hours; it is much bigger than it looks from the car park, and a lot of it is outdoors and spread between buildings, so heavy rain does spoil it. Admission has generally been valid for two consecutive days, which is worth knowing if you run out of afternoon. Check the current price and hours before setting off, because both change season to season.

items.name: Great Adirondack Moose Festival
items.what: A small-town autumn festival over a weekend in late September: craft and vendor stalls, a moose calling contest, guided moose-spotting outings and a run of children's competitions.
items.note: 26 and 27 September in 2026; confirm the date each year with the Indian Lake Chamber, as it moves with the calendar. Free to attend. It lands on what is often the best foliage weekend of the year and on the same weekend as the Adirondack Marathon, so Routes 28 and 30 are busier than usual and parking in the hamlet is limited — go early. Bring cash for the stalls and a proper coat: late September mornings at that elevation are cold.

items.name: Gore Mountain Harvest Fest and autumn Skyrides
items.what: A free autumn fair at the ski base with craft stalls, live music and food, paired with paid gondola rides up the mountain for the foliage view. The Skyrides also run on selected weekends either side of the festival, without the crowds.
items.note: Harvest Fest is 10 and 11 October 2026, 10am to 4pm. Admission and parking are free, the gondola is not — check the current ticket price, and note that Skyride sales stop at 3pm with the last ride up at 3.15pm, so this is not an afternoon-nap day. The summit is far colder and windier than the base, so take proper coats even in mild weather. Skyride weekends outside the festival are weather-dependent and can be cancelled for wind, so check the day before. Gore is also the region's main winter draw, running roughly late November to early April depending on snow.

items.name: Hudson River Whitewater Derby
items.what: One of the oldest continuously running whitewater races in the country, dating to 1958. Slalom racing on the Saturday at North Creek, a downriver race of about 7.5 miles on the Sunday, plus a small street event. Free to watch from the riverbank.
items.note: Held the first full weekend of May, which is exactly when the Hudson is highest, fastest and coldest. Confirm on the Visit North Creek page that it is running and which races are on before planning round it: individual races have been cancelled in past years for high water or lack of entries. Free for spectators, but riverfront parking fills early and it is easier to walk in from the village. Early May here can be close to freezing and sleeting — dress for winter and bring a flask. Not much use for anyone who cannot stand outside for a couple of hours.

items.name: Lake George village
items.what: An old-fashioned lake resort strip: steamboat cruises, mini-golf, arcades, sweet shops and a long public beach. It is the right answer on the day when teenagers have had enough forest, and the wrong answer on any other day.
items.note: Almost everything on Canada Street shuts from about November to April, so out of season this is a walk by a cold lake. The exception is the Winter Carnival, free, held across five weekends from early February into early March (it ran 7 February to 8 March in 2026 — get the coming year's dates before you rely on them), with outhouse races, ice events and Saturday fireworks; the on-ice events only happen if the lake actually freezes. Avoid the village entirely during Americade, the motorcycle rally at the end of May, and the Adirondack Nationals car show in the second week of September — both fill every road and car park for days — unless those are why you came. Both dates move each year; check before booking anything around them.

items.name: Adirondack Balloon Festival
items.what: More than sixty hot air balloons launching from Floyd Bennett Memorial Airport over four days in the third week of September, with an opening evening at Crandall Park in Glens Falls. Free to attend and free to park.
items.note: 17 to 20 September in 2026: opening night at Crandall Park on the Thursday, the airport launches Friday to Sunday. The launches worth the trip are the early morning one and the early evening one; the middle of the day is a field with food stalls. Traffic into the airport is severe, so leave an hour earlier than seems sensible and expect a long walk from the parking field. Standard parking is free; a paid premium pass exists if you want to be close. Launches are scrubbed outright for wind or rain and frequently are, so treat any single slot as a maybe and check the festival's own updates that morning. Riding in a balloon is a separate paid arrangement and books out well ahead.

items.name: Saratoga Springs as a day trip
items.what: The one place within an hour that is a real small city rather than a resort: a walkable Broadway with bookshops, restaurants and bars that keep normal hours, Congress Park, the thoroughbred racecourse, SPAC for concerts and the Philadelphia Orchestra, and Saratoga Spa State Park with mineral springs, trails, a car museum and public baths.
items.note: The summer race meet runs from early July to Labor Day — 3 July to 7 September in 2026 — and the dates shift each year, so check NYRA before planning a stay around it. General admission is cheap and usually available on the day, but reserved seats, big Saturday cards and Travers Day sell out months ahead, and lodging across the whole region tightens on those weekends. SPAC lawn tickets are often available late; amphitheatre seats are not. Race-day parking downtown is the main headache, so arrive early or use the garages. In winter the town is quieter but not dead: museums, the state park's ski and snowshoe trails, and holiday lights in Congress Park.
items.needs_booking: essential for big race days and SPAC seats, months ahead; nothing else needs it

categories.intro: Wevertown is a crossroads hamlet, not a town: the supermarket, pharmacy, liquor store, hardware shop, bank and petrol are all about ten minutes away in North Creek, and the nearest emergency room is roughly fifty minutes. Sort out food, fuel, cash and firewood on your first afternoon, because the pharmacy is shut at weekends, both hardware shops are shut on Sunday, the ski shop is shut midweek, and seasonal hours change without notice.

items.name: Tops Friendly Market, North Creek
items.what: The only proper supermarket within half an hour, at 273 Main Street. Full produce, meat, deli counter, beer, nappies, basic household goods. Enough to stock a five-bedroom house for a week.
items.note: It is a small-town store. Anything specific — a particular cut of meat, gluten-free bread, fresh fish, a wide choice of wine — bring it with you or buy it in Queensbury on the drive up. New York supermarkets cannot sell wine or spirits, only beer and cider; the liquor store for wine is Adirondack Spirits in the same Main Street row, and it does open on Sunday afternoons. Listed hours have run early morning to evening Monday to Saturday and shorter on Sunday, but check before a late run.

items.name: Kelly's Good Eats and More, Wevertown
items.what: Deli, pizza and small country store at 2378 Route 28, the nearest shop of any kind to the house. Breakfast sandwiches, subs, pizza, wings, basic groceries. Take-away.
items.note: This is the building that used to be Full Belly Deli, which has closed — older guidebooks, maps and signage still name Full Belly, so do not assume the deli has gone. Kelly's has been listed open seven days with earlier closing Monday to Thursday than at the weekend, but a one-till in a hamlet closes when it closes; ring or check its Facebook page the morning you want breakfast rather than driving down with five hungry children. It is a five-minute drive, not a walk.

items.name: Stewart's Shops (petrol, ice, milk, ice cream)
items.what: The regional convenience chain and the practical petrol stop. The North Creek shop is on Route 28; there is another in Chestertown. Fuel, coffee, ice, milk, cheap ice cream by the scoop, and a cash machine.
items.note: There is no petrol station in Wevertown itself. Fill up in North Creek or Chestertown rather than running low — the stretch of Route 28 west towards Indian Lake has long gaps and what stations there are keep short hours. Fuel is noticeably cheaper down in Warrensburg and Queensbury, so top up on the way in. Stewart's keeps longer hours than anything else locally, which makes it the fallback when the supermarket has shut, but check the closing time rather than assuming it is open all night.

items.name: Walgreens Pharmacy, North Creek
items.what: The nearest pharmacy, at 284 Main Street, a short walk along from the supermarket. Prescriptions plus the usual over-the-counter stock.
items.note: This is the single biggest thing to get wrong. It has been listed as open weekday daytimes only and closed both Saturday and Sunday, with the pharmacy counter also shut for a lunch break. Do not arrive on a Friday night expecting to collect a prescription on Saturday. Bring every regular medication with you in sufficient quantity. If you do need a pharmacy at the weekend, the nearest realistic option is the pharmacy beside the Warrensburg Health Center, twenty-five minutes the other way. Walgreens has been closing rural branches nationally, so confirm this one is still trading before you count on it.

items.name: Warrensburg Health Center Urgent Care
items.what: Hudson Headwaters walk-in urgent care at 3767 Main Street, open seven days with evening hours. The right place for a sprained ankle, a ski-day wrist, stitches, an ear infection or a chest cold. Walk-ins welcome, not just registered patients.
items.note: Listed hours have run Monday to Saturday into the evening and a shorter Sunday, but check the same day. First come, first served, and the wait after a busy ski Saturday can be long. A pharmacy sits next door, which is the practical reason to come here rather than to the North Creek clinic if you need a prescription filled the same day — and the reason it is worth the twenty-five minutes at a weekend, when North Creek's pharmacy is shut.

items.name: North Creek Health Center
items.what: Hudson Headwaters primary care clinic at 126 Ski Bowl Road. The closest medical help to the house for something that is not an emergency. Listed as weekdays plus a Saturday morning.
items.note: This is a primary care office, not an urgent care and not an emergency room. Ring first on 518-251-2541 and ask whether they can see a visitor the same day. If they cannot, the answer is Warrensburg urgent care — which is not "a bit further on" but twenty-five minutes in the opposite direction from the house, so decide which way you are driving before you set off with a sick child in the car.

items.name: Glens Falls Hospital Emergency Department
items.what: The nearest full emergency room, at 100 Park Street, open 24 hours. Part of the Albany Med system. This is where an ambulance from Johnsburg will take you.
items.note: Fifty minutes on a good day and longer in snow, so know the route before you need it. The small hospitals further north are further from the house, not nearer, so this is the answer in every direction. For anything genuinely serious call 911 and let the Johnsburg and North Creek volunteer squads come to you rather than driving yourself. Mobile signal at the house may not be good enough to make that call — ask the owner before arrival whether there is a landline, and whether wifi calling works, because wifi calling only routes 911 correctly if the address has been set on the handset.

items.name: Mobile coverage, and where it fails
items.what: Coverage across the Johnsburg area is patchy and depends heavily on carrier and on which side of a hill you are standing. Some carriers work in the hamlet and not in the valleys; some are the other way round. No one can tell you in advance which will work for your phone.
items.note: Assume you will have no usable signal at the house and be pleasantly surprised. Ask the owner for the wifi details and whether wifi calling works — that is usually the real answer here. Download maps, offline routes, playlists and any booking confirmations before you leave home; Route 28 west towards Indian Lake and the back roads towards Thirteenth Lake have long dead stretches. Agree a meeting point and a time with teenagers rather than relying on being able to text them.

items.name: Braley & Noxon Hardware, North Creek
items.what: Full-service hardware shop at 256 Main Street, trading for well over a century. Housewares, plumbing bits, paint, tools, fixings, propane and someone behind the counter who knows which fitting you actually need.
items.note: Correcting a common assumption: it is Monday to Saturday and closed on Sunday. So is the lumber yard in Wevertown. That means nothing hardware-shaped is open locally on a Sunday and the nearest option is down in Warrensburg or Queensbury, the better part of an hour. Ring 518-251-2855 before driving over for anything specific. Tell the owner first about anything broken in the house — do not start fixing a rented property yourself.

items.name: T.C. Murphy Lumber, Wevertown
items.what: Lumber yard, True Value hardware and building supply at 3911 Route 8 in Wevertown, trading since 1915 and the closest trade counter to the house. Timber, hardware, paint, plumbing and electrical bits, propane and equipment hire.
items.note: Open Monday to Saturday and closed Sunday, with an early weekday close — it is a trade counter, so it shuts in the late afternoon rather than the evening. Worth ringing 518-251-2424 about firewood before you assume, and about equipment hire if you want something specific. Confirm current hours before making the trip; a hamlet lumber yard will close for a funeral or a hunting week.

items.name: Firewood
items.what: Most houses here come with a wood stove or a fire pit and some wood already stacked. Where they do not, firewood is sold locally by the face cord — ask at the Wevertown lumber yard or the North Creek hardware shop, and you will also see roadside signs and stands through the autumn.
items.note: New York restricts moving untreated firewood more than 50 miles from its source. Do not bring wood from home and do not carry it onto a state campground; buy locally sourced or kiln-dried. Ask the owner before you burn anything: some houses supply wood, some charge for it, and a few have a stove the insurer will not let guests use. Ask specifically for seasoned wood — green wood bought in a hurry will smoke and not burn. Bring long matches and firelighters, and expect the outside stack to be wet after a storm.

items.name: Cash and ATMs
items.what: Community Bank at 244 Main Street, North Creek is the only bank branch in the village and has a walk-up cash machine. There is also a machine in the Stewart's on Route 28. Arrow Bank, the rebranded Glens Falls National, has a branch in Chestertown about fifteen minutes away.
items.note: Carry cash. Farm stands, some diners, firewood sellers, trailhead parking and a few small shops are cash-only or cash-preferred, and card readers in the valley go down when the line does. The bank lobby is weekdays only, so at a weekend you are relying on the walk-up machine or the one in Stewart's, and the convenience-store machine charges a fee. Take out what you need for the week in one go rather than making a special trip.

items.name: Ski and snowboard hire
items.what: Cunningham's Ski Barn at 1 Main Street, North Creek does alpine and cross-country hire, snowshoes, repairs and tuning. Adirondack All Seasons Outfitters on Route 28 also hires skis and boards. Beaver Brook in Wevertown does daily, weekly and seasonal ski hire. Gore Mountain rents at the base lodge, and Garnet Hill in North River is the cross-country specialist with its own trail network.
items.note: Cunningham's has run closed on Tuesdays and Wednesdays, which catches midweek arrivals out — check the day before you plan to collect kit. Hiring in the village is cheaper than hiring at the mountain and you keep the kit for the week instead of queueing every morning; ask for the weekly rate rather than paying by the day. Book ahead for a group of six or more before a holiday weekend. Bring your own helmets and goggles if you can — hire helmets in children's sizes are the first thing to run out at half-term.

items.name: Bike, kayak and canoe hire
items.what: Beaver Brook Outfitters, on Route 28 between Wevertown and North Creek, hires canoes, kayaks and tubes to take away, with multi-day rates, and also runs guided Hudson River rafting and tubing trips. Adirondack All Seasons Outfitters in North Creek hires bikes and boats in summer.
items.note: Beaver Brook is the closest outfitter to the house, a few minutes up the road. Ring ahead in July and August — a family-sized set of boats on a hot Saturday goes early. Check whether the price includes roof-rack straps and buoyancy aids, and whether they will deliver to a put-in, because getting three boats onto a hire car is the usual sticking point. Hire bikes here are hardtails and hybrids, not full-suspension mountain bikes. Guided whitewater rafting on the Hudson is a spring high-water activity with minimum ages; it is not the same thing as hiring a canoe for the lake.

items.name: Laundry
items.what: Warrensburg Laundry & Dry Cleaning at 11 Richards Avenue is the nearest established laundry business, with self-service machines as well as drop-off wash-and-fold and dry cleaning.
items.note: Twenty-five minutes each way makes this an errand, not a quick job — pair it with the Warrensburg shops, the pharmacy or urgent care. Check before setting off that the self-service side is open that day and take plenty of quarters. Listings for a laundromat in North Creek itself are inconsistent and may be out of date, so do not drive there on spec. For a week with twelve people the simpler answer is to check with the owner what the house washer and dryer can actually cope with, and bring extra detergent.

items.name: Vet, routine and emergency
items.what: Schroon River Animal Hospital at 150 Schroon River Road, Warrensburg is the nearest small-animal practice, listed as weekdays only and closed at weekends. The nearest after-hours emergency clinic is at Gansevoort, south of Glens Falls, which is over an hour from the house.
items.note: The weekend is the problem. The local practice is weekdays only, and published hours for the Gansevoort emergency clinic have been contradictory — some sources say 24 hours seven days, others show it closed for part of the midweek. Ring before you drive anywhere, and expect over an hour to get there. If you are travelling with a dog on chronic medication, bring more than you need, because you cannot rely on getting a prescription filled here at short notice. Keep dogs leashed on trails: a face full of porcupine quills at 9pm is the classic Adirondack holiday vet bill.

items.name: Winter driving reality
items.what: Routes 28 and 8 are state roads, plowed early and well, and generally driveable through a storm. The problem is the last mile: side roads and private lake roads are plowed later, plowed to a packed-snow surface rather than to tarmac, and can be steep and icy for days after a storm.
items.note: Between roughly December and March, a two-wheel-drive car on all-season tyres is not enough here. Bring or hire a car with all-wheel drive or proper winter tyres. Ask the owner directly how the driveway and the access road are plowed, and whether an ordinary saloon has made it up in past winters — get that answer before you book, not on arrival at 9pm in the dark. Keep a shovel, a scraper, a torch and a blanket in the boot. North Creek can have eight inches of snow while Albany airport has none, so allow well over the usual 75 minutes for an airport run in winter. Black ice on shaded bends in the late afternoon is the commonest way visitors come off the road.

items.name: Black flies, ticks, and bears
items.what: Three seasonal realities a first-time visitor will not expect. Black flies swarm from roughly mid-May to late June and are worst near running water on still, warm, overcast days. Deer ticks are present and Lyme disease occurs in Warren County. Black bears are common in Johnsburg and are opportunists around rubbish.
items.note: For black flies bring a head net per person and a repellent that works — DEET or picaridin; citronella wristbands do nothing. Long sleeves and light colours help; the flies bite at the hairline and the back of the neck. For ticks, do a full body check every evening, especially on children and behind knees, and carry a proper tick remover rather than tweezers. Treating trousers with permethrin before you travel is worth the effort. For bears, never leave rubbish, cool boxes, barbecue grease or dog food outside or on a screened porch overnight; bins go in a garage or a locked shed, and the bin lid is not a deterrent. A bear that finds food at a house comes back every night for the rest of your stay and the one after.

items.name: What people forget to bring
items.what: The running list of things guests end up driving half an hour to buy, or doing without.
items.note: Prescription medicines in full, because the local pharmacy is shut at weekends. A torch or head torch per person — power cuts happen in storms and there are no street lights. Insect repellent and head nets from May to July. Sun cream, which people skip in winter and then burn on snow. Swimming shoes for the lake bottom. A tick remover and a basic first-aid kit. Paper maps or downloaded offline maps. Cash. Bin bags and washing-up liquid if the house does not restock them. Board games and a couple of DVDs for a rain day, since streaming depends on rural internet that may be slow. Adapters and a power strip: five bedrooms and twelve people is about twenty devices and not enough sockets. A cool box for the drive up, so the supermarket run does not have to happen twice.
